candidate.derivedAnswer: C: Order matters in a sequence, while order does not matter in a set of numbers
candidate.answerReason: A sequence assigns numbers to ordered positions, whereas changing the listing order of a set does not change the set.

methods.label: Use the ordered nature of a sequence
methods.explanation: A sequence is arranged in order. Rearranging the same numbers generally gives a different sequence.
methods.levelReason: Uses the definitions of sequences and order-independent set listings.
